original_question: Fix an interval I contained in R and a subset B contained in R. Can one construct a family of measures {mu_beta} such that for every subset J of I the singular part of mu_beta gives J positive mass exactly for parameters beta in B, while the absolutely continuous part of mu_beta gives J positive mass for every beta in R?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open problem in the discussion of instability of singular spectrum, immediately after the paper recalls the Del Rio-Fuentes-Poltoratskii result and asks whether one can replace 'almost every' by 'every' when prescribing the perturbation parameters for which dense singular spectrum occurs on an interval I.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the main ingredients of the targeted problem: an interval I in R, a parameter set B in R, a real-parameter family of measures indexed by beta, and the idea that the singular versus absolutely continuous behavior should distinguish beta in B from beta outside B.
missing_details: The measures are not arbitrary; they are spectral measures of a family of rank-one perturbations A_beta = A + beta(·,phi)phi associated with a cyclic vector phi.
The paper requires B to be a measurable subset of R, not just an arbitrary subset.
The quantifier is over all beta in R; the point of the open problem is to improve an earlier 'almost every beta' realization theorem to an 'every beta' statement.
The official target is 'dense singular spectrum on I', not the much stronger condition that the singular part assign positive mass to every subset J of I.
Outside B, the paper asks for the corresponding operator to have purely absolutely continuous spectrum on I, not merely for the absolutely continuous part to be nonzero or positive on every test set.

The surrounding context is dense singular spectrum embedded in absolutely continuous spectrum; the paper is not posing a free-standing measure-realization problem detached from rank-one perturbation/Clark theory.
No auxiliary quantification over subsets J of I appears in the paper's formulation; the problem is stated directly in terms of spectral type on I.

The notation mu_beta should be understood as the spectral measure of the perturbed operator with respect to the distinguished cyclic vector, not just any decomposition mu_beta = (mu_beta)_ac + (mu_beta)_s.
refined_question: Let I be an interval in R and let B be a measurable subset of R. Does there exist a family {mu_beta}_{beta in R} of spectral measures arising from a family of rank-one perturbations such that, for every beta in B, the corresponding perturbation has singular spectrum dense in I and embedded there in absolutely continuous spectrum, while for every beta in R\B the corresponding operator has purely absolutely continuous spectrum on I?
justification: The draft is trying to encode the paper's open problem about prescribing exactly which perturbation parameters produce dense singular spectrum on a fixed interval. The nearby setup defines the relevant family as spectral measures mu_alpha of self-adjoint rank-one perturbations A_alpha = A + alpha(·,phi)phi with phi cyclic, and explains that the absolutely continuous parts of the mu_alpha are mutually absolutely continuous while the singular parts are mutually singular. Against that setup, the closest official formulation is the unnumbered open problem asking whether one can realize a measurable set B exactly as the set of parameters for which dense singular spectrum occurs on I, with purely absolutely continuous spectrum on I outside B. Your draft is therefore directionally right, but it replaces the paper's spectral-type statement by a substantially stronger and different condition involving positive mass on every subset J of I.
